electionHistory.text: 2002 general, Hillsborough County Commission District 2: Won (first elected). County page says first elected in 2002. Official 2002 results are not on the SOE results archive, so vote share is not available.

2006 general, Hillsborough County Commission District 2: Kept seat; no District 2 contest appears in the official 2006 primary or general results. Neighborhood News reports he held District 2 from 2002 to 2010. The SOE results do not say whether he was unopposed.
2010 general, Hillsborough County Commission District 5 (countywide): Won. Linda Saul-Sena (DEM) 42.49% (131,504); Jim Hosler (NPA) 4.83% (14,957). No District 5 contest in the 2010 primary results.

2014 general, Hillsborough County Commission District 5 (countywide): Re-elected. Osprey Observer (Dec 17, 2014) calls him re-elected for Countywide District 5. SOE ENR pages soe-2014p and soe-2014g list no District 5 race.
2018 Republican primary, Hillsborough County Commission District 2: Won. Chris Paradies 27.6% (7,504).
2018 general, Hillsborough County Commission District 2: Won. Angela Birdsong (D) 47.6% (67,378).
2022 general, Hillsborough County Commission District 2: Won. Angela Birdsong (D) 43.4% (54,444). Republican primary canceled.
2024 Republican primary, Hillsborough County Commission District 2: Won. Melissa Nordbeck 21.8% (4,188).
2024 general, Hillsborough County Commission District 2: Won. Patricia Altagracia Alonzo (D) 44.9% (74,084). Term ends 2028.

Aug 28, 2026: Before the Rays vote he said: "To be a world-class community requires vision, courage, bold leadership, and the ability to think big."

Apr 17, 2024: Voted no on enacting the ordinance setting the Community Investment Tax renewal referendum (RCS 4308, Ordinance 24-3; Hagan and Kemp voted no).
Jul 17, 2024: Voted no on approving the School Board's Nov 5, 2024 referendum for additional operating property taxes (RCS 4437; 3 yes, 4 no).
Apr 20, 2022: Voted no on placing the 1 percent transportation surtax ordinance on the Nov 8, 2022 ballot (RCS 3284, Ordinance 22-9).
May 4, 2022: Voted no on the resolution calling the Aug 23, 2022 School Board referendum (RCS 3299).
May 8, 2025: Only no vote on transmitting an Urban Service Area expansion of about 295.6 acres on Lutz Lake Fern Road (RCS 4886).

Dec 3, 2025: County page calls him the board's leading voice for a Rays ballpark in Ybor City and credits him with creating the Tampa/Hillsborough Film Commission.
Dec 20, 2013: PolitiFact rated Mostly False his Dec 2013 claim that studies suggest the 2017 College Football Playoff championship game would bring about 1,700 to 1,800 full-time jobs.

conflicts.text: Ethics complaint 14-124 resolved by stipulation (final order 14-117) on Article II, Section 8 of the Florida Constitution (financial disclosure).
Florida Politics reports the 2014 complaint led Hagan to pay a $2,000 fine for failing to properly disclose assets on financial disclosure forms.

Aug 2014: the Commission on Ethics agreed to investigate a complaint by George Niemann that Hagan's disclosure listed an investment account ($401,000) and retirement accounts ($219,000) without naming specific assets. Hagan called the complaint "laughable".

A complaint by Niemann and three others alleging free campaign help from consultant Beth Leytham in connection with a Go Hillsborough contract was dismissed by the Commission on Ethics; the Sheriff's Office found no criminal violations in 2016 (as reported).

votes.headline: Approved $75 million for ZooTampa renovations and expansion
votes.inShort: The county will pay ZooTampa $5 million a year through 2041 from Community Investment Tax (half-cent sales tax) money, and the zoo must match it, for $150 million in upgrades and a new South America section. Some commissioners argued the money should be shared with other cultural groups.

does.text: The board approved this package 4 to 3 on Oct 21, 2026, after a public hearing, with Commissioners Cohen, Hagan and Myers voting no; on Oct 7 it had voted 4 to 3 to move toward finalizing the agreement. Approves a 15-year agreement under which the county pays ZooTampa up to $75 million, $5 million a year through 2041, from Community Investment Tax money (a half-cent sales tax), and the zoo matches it one to one, for about $150 million of work. The plan includes upgrades to older habitats, an expanded elephant habitat, a family coaster and a new South America section that extends across North Boulevard onto about 14 acres now used as a City of Tampa maintenance lot. Some commissioners questioned why other eligible groups such as the Children's Museum, Tampa Bay History Center and Straz Center got nothing from this package, while others noted that the same fund sends far more to the Rays stadium, per Bay News 9.

after.text: A majority of the board voted to add ZooTampa capital improvements to the list of projects paid for by the renewed Community Investment Tax. The board also approved an FY 2027 budget amendment putting $5,000,000 in the CIT Extension Project Fund for ZooTampa.

votes.headline: Gave final approval to county funding for a new Rays ballpark
votes.inShort: At a special meeting, the commission approved the development and funding agreement, guaranty and team non-relocation agreement for a Rays ballpark on Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus. The county's share is capped at $796 million, and the Rays cover more than $1.3 billion plus cost overruns.

does.text: Approves the Development and Funding Agreement, a guaranty and a team non-relocation agreement for a Rays ballpark and mixed-use district on Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus, at Dale Mabry Highway and West Tampa Bay Boulevard. WUSF reported that the county's share is capped at $796 million, including $360 million from the Community Investment Tax (a half-cent sales tax), $263 million backed by the tourist development tax, $103 million in other county funds and $30 million in federal disaster-recovery money (those listed amounts total $756 million; WUSF did not explain the difference), while the Rays pay more than $1.3 billion plus all cost overruns. The county said the Rays plan to open the ballpark in April 2029, and that the board still had to approve a ballpark license and use agreement, a community benefits agreement and a construction funds trust agreement.

after.text: A majority of the board approved an interlocal agreement making the Tampa Sports Authority the county's representative under the Development and Funding Agreement. The authority will oversee design documents, construction materials, schedules and budgets for the stadium.

votes.headline: Approved changes to the proposed FY 2027 budget
votes.inShort: At a budget reconciliation hearing on a recommended $14.1 billion FY 2027 budget, commissioners voted on items they had flagged for change. The plan included a millage swap to support public safety and other county services.

does.text: At the July 29 budget reconciliation hearing, commissioners voted 7 to 0 to approve changes to items they had flagged in the recommended FY 2027 budget, which the county described as a proposed $14.1 billion budget, including a millage swap to support public safety and other services, per a Govly meeting summary. The summary says the board discussed moving money from some nonprofits back to county departments for local infrastructure, but it does not list the individual changes or the tax rates. The vote applied to the recommended budget; the final FY 2027 budget and tax rates were adopted later.

after.text: The county's property tax page, last updated Oct 16, 2026, said the adopted FY 2027 budget cut the countywide property tax rate to 5.3608 mills, down from 5.4608 in FY 2026, and set the unincorporated-area rate at 4.7163 mills. It said about 70% of the adopted unincorporated-area general fund goes to public safety.

votes.headline: Approved a non-binding deal to pursue a new Rays ballpark in Tampa
votes.inShort: The commission approved a non-binding memorandum of understanding with the Tampa Bay Rays and the City of Tampa for a ballpark and mixed-use district on Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus. It set the terms the final contracts would follow.

does.text: Approves a non-binding memorandum of understanding with the Tampa Bay Rays and the City of Tampa for a ballpark and mixed-use district on Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus. It passed 5 to 2 on May 20, 2026. Because it was non-binding, it set the terms for the final contracts but did not commit county money by itself; the final agreements came up for a separate vote in August. WWSB reported a total project cost of about $2.3 billion and a county share in the MOU of up to $796 million ($360 million Community Investment Tax, more than $260 million in tourist tax bonds and $103 million in other county funds).

after.text: The Tampa City Council approved the city's part of the final stadium deal 4 to 3.

The County Commission voted 5 to 2 to approve the Development and Funding Agreement, guaranty and team non-relocation agreement, with the county's share capped at $796 million. WUSF reported that figure was $100 million less than the May MOU.
A majority of the board approved an interlocal agreement with the Tampa Sports Authority to act as the county's representative under the Development and Funding Agreement.
